eli: Kicked off the Silverpine POC mixed-workload run this morning. Seeing brief 95/99th tail latency spikes (~600-900ms) while median stays ~85ms. QPS ~1.2k sustained with microbursts up to 3k. Anyone seen this pattern?
rina: Yikes. Can you paste the load profile and batch config?
eli: Load profile: mixture of short (seq 64) embed requests + long (seq 512) chat generations. Traffic ratio ~65/35. Serving pool: 4x A10g-like GPUs (dedicated), model pinned to open-llama-13b-4bit, batching = continuous, max_batch_tokens=2048, batch_timeout_ms=15.
jamal: Do the spikes align with the long requests? Could be KV cache misses when sequences switch.
eli: Not always. We saw spikes also during short request floods. Attached sample logs: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:03:10Z] req_id=abc123 worker=slot-2 qlen=7 batch_tokens=1600 p99=780ms gpu_util=73% kvcache_hits=0.87
[2026-03-12T14:03:11Z] req_id=abc160 worker=slot-3 qlen=2 batch_tokens=320 p99=120ms gpu_util=40% kvcache_hits=0.92
[2026-03-12T14:03:12Z] req_id=abc200 worker=slot-1 qlen=12 batch_tokens=2500 p99=880ms gpu_util=95% kvcache_hits=0.54
```
eli: Notice the drop in kvcache_hits right before the big p99.
ops-bot: autoscaler: noted CPU/GPU headroom low at 14:03:12; no scale-up triggered because reserved capacity hit.
infra-luis: If reserved/dedicated pool is at commit, autoscaler won't add more. That could explain queueing/backpressure. Did the customer request burst beyond committed capacity?
sales-amy: Silverpine asked for burst window in contract but not enabled in this test — we kept them on reserved capacity only. They asked for pricing for burst yesterday.
jamal: Two likely causes: 1) KV cache eviction when long contexts flood memory -> cold KV sequences + large batches cause GPU mem pressure and stalls. 2) Batching path: very large batches (batch_tokens>max) causing multiple inner loops and increased scheduling jitter.
rina: Can we reproduce with a focused test? Run a 10min mixed run where we toggle prefix-caching off/on and compare p99. Also try decreasing batch_timeout_ms to 7 and increase max_batch_tokens to 4096 for a run.
eli: Running reproducer now: command I'm using: 
```
./loadgen --target 1200 --burst 3000 --mix "short:0.65:seq=64, long:0.35:seq=512" --duration 600 --tag silverpine-03
```
eli: Also firing a micro run with prefix_cache disabled:
```
POST /admin/cache/config
{"prefix_cache_enabled": false}
```
jamal: If the reproducer shows p99 drop when caching is enabled, then it's likely eviction thrash. If disabling caching helps but GPU util drops, we might be hitting scheduling inefficiencies.
infra-luis: I'll pull kernel-level GPU metrics and NVLink stats for that window. Also check for PCIe throttles.
sales-amy: Silverpine wants clarification: will enabling burst pricing & temporary dedicated autoscaling remove these spikes or just reduce blocked requests? Need a concise answer for the contract.
jamal: Short answer: burst autoscaling will reduce queueing/backpressure by adding capacity during spikes (reduces observed p99 caused by saturation). But if root cause is KV cache eviction due to context churn, autoscaling alone won't eliminate cold-cache stalls; caching+hot-warm routing + model-pin for long contexts helps.
rina: Proposed immediate mitigations for the POC: 1) enable prefix caching (tune cache size), 2) add a hot-route that pins long-context requests to a small warm pool (lower kv churn), 3) temporarily allow burst autoscaling for the next run, 4) test batch_timeout_ms=7 and max_batch_tokens=4096.
eli: Results from first reproducer (10:04 run): with prefix_cache off -> p99 median=320ms, but occasional 720ms spikes; with prefix_cache on -> p99 median=110ms, but occasional 880ms spikes at different times.
jamal: Interesting — suggests caching helps overall but still subject to occasional high-cost ops (maybe large generation windows finishing). Can you dump per-request sequence length distribution and token generation time?
eli: Pushed CSV to shared drive: shows 6% of requests generate >256 tokens and those line up with ~70% of big spikes.
nina (typo corrected): (no message)
infra-luis: From GPU traces I pulled: there are periodic context-switch stalls when a large generation starts in a worker that had small cached KV; we see memcpy spikes. NVLink throughput at those times saturates.
sales-amy: So for customer-facing summary: we should tell Silverpine that we can materially reduce median and tail with caching + routing + burst autoscale, but for rare very long generations we still recommend setting a soft limit or graceful fallback (streaming with chunked outputs) to avoid single-request-driven tail spikes.
eli: Next steps I've scheduled: 1) enable temporary burst autoscale for next run (ops), 2) implement hot-route for long contexts (infra), 3) run 30m validation with customer traffic pattern, 4) put a short note for pricing team re: burst cost estimate.
ops-bot: change_request: enable_burst_autoscale(silverpine-poc) submitted by eli at 2026-03-12T14:20:34Z — pending approval from infra-luis.
infra-luis: Approved, enabling now.
sales-amy: I'll prepare a one-paragraph explanation + ballpark burst cost for Silverpine: estimate ~+$0.08/min during the burst window at expected 30min/day across 2 weekdays.
eli: Thanks — I'll run the 30m and post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
jamal: If we need ops' help with deeper profiling, ping me and I'll instrument extra traces. :mag:
eli: Posting results follow-up shortly.
